shortsPnl() was modified to use Math.abs(sh[id].qty)
The formula used in shortsPnl() is (avg - current) * qty
Previously, a negative-qty short position would flip the sign of the P&L calculation in shortsPnl()
A negative-qty short would distort the P&L for that position under the old implementation
Using Math.abs(sh[id].qty) produces the correct magnitude and sign even if a short position's qty is stored as a negative number
Every other short-related function besides shortsPnl() was left untouched
